html:
When you’re looking to boost flavor without spending extra time, herb scissors mini herb butter cubes are a game changer. The five‑blade Herb Scissors let you chop cilantro, chives, basil, and other fresh herbs in a single snip, then mix them straight into softened butter. The result is perfectly seasoned butter that you can portion into bite‑size cubes, freeze, and toss onto grilled veggies, steaks, or toast whenever you need a burst of freshness.

Why Mini Herb‑Infused Butter Cubes Are Worth the Effort

Mini butter cubes are more than a garnish; they’re a versatile flavor base. A single cube can melt into a pan, melt over a baked potato, or be dropped onto a steaming pile of rice for instant herb‑infused richness. Because they’re frozen, you can keep a variety of herb blends on hand without worrying about waste. The key to a smooth, even distribution of herbs is a fine mince, and that’s where herb scissors shine.

Preparing Your Herbs with Herb Scissors

Using the Herb Scissors is straightforward, but a few tricks ensure you get the best texture:

  1. Rinse and dry. Pat the herbs dry with a kitchen towel; excess water will turn butter soggy.
  2. Trim stems. For basil, remove the thick stems; for cilantro and chives, keep the tender parts.
  3. Gather in a pile. Place a handful of the herb in the scissors’ jaws.
  4. Snip repeatedly. The five blades cut the herb into a fine mince with each squeeze. Keep snipping until the pieces are uniformly small.
  5. Use the cleaning comb. After you’re done, run the comb through the blades to dislodge any stuck bits.

These steps take under a minute and produce a consistent mince that blends seamlessly into butter.

Mixing Herbs Into Butter

Start with room‑temperature butter so it incorporates easily. Here’s a reliable method:

  • Place 1/2 cup (1 stick) of softened butter in a medium bowl.
  • Add the minced herbs from the Herb Scissors. A good rule of thumb is 1 tablespoon of herb per stick of butter, but feel free to adjust.
  • Optional: Add a pinch of salt, a squeeze of lemon juice, or a dash of garlic powder for extra depth.
  • Use a rubber spatula to fold the herbs into the butter until evenly distributed.

For a smoother texture, you can also use a hand mixer on low speed for 30 seconds, but the manual fold works just fine and keeps the herb’s bright color intact.

Portioning and Freezing the Butter Cubes

Once the herb butter is fully mixed, it’s time to form the mini cubes. Silicone ice cube trays work best because they release the butter easily.

Steps:

  1. Spoon the herb butter into each compartment, filling just below the top.
  2. Cover the tray with plastic wrap to prevent freezer burn.
  3. Freeze for 2–3 hours, or until solid.
  4. Pop the cubes out and transfer them to an airtight freezer bag.

Label the bag with the herb blend and date. Properly stored, the cubes stay fresh for up to three months.

Creative Ways to Use Herb‑Infused Butter Cubes

Having these cubes on hand opens up a world of quick flavor upgrades:

  • Steak or chicken. Drop a cube onto a hot grill‑cooked piece; it melts, forming a glossy, aromatic glaze.
  • Vegetable roasts. Toss cubed potatoes, carrots, or asparagus with a butter cube before roasting for caramelized herbs.
  • Seafood. Place a cube on a pan‑seared salmon fillet for a buttery herb finish.
  • Breakfast. Melt a cube into scrambled eggs or on top of toasted sourdough for a bright start.
  • Grains. Stir a cube into hot quinoa, rice, or couscous for instant flavor.

The possibilities are endless, and because each cube is pre‑measured, you never over‑season.

Cleaning and Maintaining Your Herb Scissors

The Herb Scissors come with a handy cleaning comb, which makes upkeep a breeze. After each use, rinse the blades under warm water, then run the comb through to dislodge any lingering herb fibers. For stubborn residue, a quick soak in soapy water followed by a thorough rinse will keep the blades sharp. Dry the scissors promptly to prevent rust.

FAQ

Can I use frozen herbs with the Herb Scissors?

It’s best to use fresh, thawed herbs. Frozen herbs tend to be watery and can cling to the blades, making a clean cut difficult.

How long do the herb‑infused butter cubes stay fresh?

When stored in an airtight freezer bag, the cubes retain optimal flavor for about three months. After that, they’re still safe but may lose some herb vibrancy.

Is the Herb Scissors suitable for tougher herbs like rosemary?

The five‑blade design works best with softer herbs such as cilantro, chives, and basil. For tougher, woody herbs like rosemary, a traditional knife or a dedicated herb chopper yields better results.
